title: Bariloche: lakes, mountains and forests
meta_description: Bariloche guide: Circuito Chico, Cerro Campanario, Victoria Island, skiing at Catedral, how to get there and where to stay.
hero_subtitle: On the shores of Lake Nahuel Huapi, a year-round destination.
photo_alt: Lake Nahuel Huapi surrounded by mountains

why_visit.title: Nahuel Huapi National Park
why_visit.text: Lakes, forests and mountains inside Argentina's oldest national park.

why_visit.title: Snow in winter
why_visit.text: Cerro Catedral is one of South America's best-known ski resorts.

why_visit.title: Food
why_visit.text: Chocolate, craft beer and mountain dishes with trout and venison.

activities.title: Circuito Chico
activities.text: The classic drive along Nahuel Huapi to the Llao Llao Peninsula, by car, bike or tour.

activities.title: Cerro Campanario
activities.text: A chairlift takes you up in minutes to one of the area's best panoramic views.

activities.title: Victoria Island and Arrayanes Forest
activities.text: A boat trip from Puerto Pañuelo to the island and the cinnamon-barked arrayán forest.

activities.title: Cerro Catedral
activities.text: Skiing in winter and, in summer, lifts and trails such as the one to Refugio Frey.

activities.title: Mount Tronador
activities.text: A full-day trip to the area's highest mountain and the Ventisquero Negro glacier.

how_to_get_there:
By plane: Bariloche International Airport (BRC) has direct flights from Buenos Aires, about two hours, and from other cities.

By bus: long-distance services run from Buenos Aires and other cities; the trip from the capital takes about a day.

From Chile: overland via the Cardenal Samoré Pass, which links the area with Osorno and Puerto Montt.

where_to_stay.budget: Hostels with shared rooms and guest kitchens, plus campsites in season. They're the most affordable option and a good place to meet other travelers.
where_to_stay.midrange: Inns, cabins and small hotels, often with breakfast included. Cabins with kitchens suit families and groups.
where_to_stay.luxury: Upscale hotels and lodges with landscape views, spas or tours included. Book them well in advance.

practical_tips.title: Best time
practical_tips.text: Summer for lakes and hiking; winter for snow. January and July are the busiest months.

practical_tips.title: Changeable weather
practical_tips.text: Wind and sudden weather changes are part of the trip. Dress in layers and always carry a windbreaker.

practical_tips.title: Book ahead
practical_tips.text: In high season, lodging and tours fill up. It's best to book as soon as you have your dates.

practical_tips.title: Prices and payments
practical_tips.text: Prices change often: check current rates before you travel and carry some cash as well as cards.

closing: Bariloche works as a base for exploring the Lake District, including the Seven Lakes Road to San Martín de los Andes.
